pairs.label: Eligibility rate
pairs.detail: Measure requests after debounce, minimum-prefix, feature consent, and local suppression.
pairs.explanation: Measure requests after debounce, minimum-prefix, feature consent, and local suppression. Raw keydown events are not server demand.

pairs.label: Concurrent work
pairs.detail: Estimate request rate multiplied by service time, then add headroom for skew, retries, deployments, and failed capacity.
pairs.explanation: Estimate request rate multiplied by service time, then add headroom for skew, retries, deployments, and failed capacity.

pairs.label: Accelerator batches
pairs.detail: Longer batch windows improve device utilization but spend freshness budget and increase tail latency.
pairs.explanation: Longer batch windows improve device utilization but spend freshness budget and increase tail latency.

pairs.label: Suggestion coverage
pairs.detail: Only a fraction of eligible requests should render.
pairs.explanation: Only a fraction of eligible requests should render. Suppression is expected, not an availability failure.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The system matters because it combines three difficult engineering problems on one path: Interactive latency: the response must feel immediate rather than merely fast on average; Selective generation: returning no suggestion is better than interrupting the writer with weak or inappropriate text; Private context: richer message and style signals can improve relevance, but each signal needs a clear purpose, scope, retention rule, and user control.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Eligibility rate: Measure requests after debounce, minimum-prefix, feature consent, and local suppression. Concurrent work: Estimate request rate multiplied by service time, then add headroom for skew, retries, deployments, and failed capacity. Accelerator batches: Longer batch windows improve device utilization but spend freshness budget and increase tail latency. Suggestion coverage: Only a fraction of eligible requests should render.

pairs.label: Current prefix
pairs.detail: Use the bounded text before the cursor plus structural markers.
pairs.explanation: Use the bounded text before the cursor plus structural markers. Preserve the exact version that candidate generation observed.

pairs.label: Conversation context
pairs.detail: Include a bounded subject or thread representation only when consent, region, retention, and quality evidence justify it.

pairs.label: Account style

pairs.explanation: Keep personalized style signals account-scoped, disableable, and separate from other users and tenants. Always retain a generic fallback.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Design overload as graceful abstention”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Queue pressure
pairs.detail: Cap queue age, dispatch partial batches, reject work that cannot meet its deadline, and ask clients to reduce request frequency.
pairs.explanation: Cap queue age, dispatch partial batches, reject work that cannot meet its deadline, and ask clients to reduce request frequency.

pairs.label: Region loss
pairs.explanation: Route only to policy-compatible regions. If failover would miss the deadline or violate residency, disable suggestions for that cohort.

pairs.label: Model failure
pairs.detail: Use a smaller compatible model or generic candidate path only when its release policy and evaluation contract are already approved.
pairs.explanation: Use a smaller compatible model or generic candidate path only when its release policy and evaluation contract are already approved.

pairs.label: Policy outage
pairs.detail: Suppress candidates when a required safety or account-scope decision cannot be made.
pairs.explanation: Suppress candidates when a required safety or account-scope decision cannot be made. Do not bypass the gate to protect coverage.
